title: Rapid biodegradation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) using effective Cronobacter sakazakii MM045 (KT933253)
author: Umar, Aziz, et al.
materials: Phenanthrene and pyrene (96%–98% purity) were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and Merck Chemicals, respectively. Other analytical grade chemicals and media were purchased from standard manufacturers and each PAH was dissolved in petroleum ether followed by filter (0.2 μm) sterilisation. Phosphate buffer saline (PBS) containing 0.24 g/L KH2PO4, 1.44 g/L Na2HPO4, 0.20 g/L KCl, 8.00 g/L NaCl, pH 7.4 was prepared using sterile deionised water. Mineral salts medium (MSM) (0.20 g/L ZnSO4•7H2O; 0.20 g/L MgSO4•7H2O, 2.00 g/L NH4Cl, 1.50 g/L KH2PO4, 9.00 g/L Na2HPO4, 10.00 μg/L CoSO4•7H2O, 3.00 g/L MnSO4•H2O, 5.00 g/L Ferric citrate, 0.01 g/L Titriplex III, pH 7.4) was prepared and employed in the biodegradation studies. Triplicate experiments were carried out for each treatment and un-inoculated media were used as negative controls.

Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrophotometer (GC–MS) analyses for each phenanthrene and pyrene were carried out using thermoscientific TG-5MS column (30 m length, 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 μm film). Helium carrier gas was injected at 1 ml/min using programmable split-less injector with an injection volume of 1 μl. The applied initial temperature of 50 °C was maintained for 3 min with the inlet temperature of 250 °C. Ramping at temperatures ranging from 10 °C to 320 °C/min was further done for 10 min. PAHs intermediate metabolites were identified by mass spectra (TQS Quantum XLS) using monitoring mode scan of 35–500 u and their comparisons to NIST database.

steps.title: Prepare PAH stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve phenanthrene (96–98 % purity, Sigma‑Aldrich) and pyrene (96–98 % purity, Merck) separately in petroleum ether, then sterilise each solution by filtration through a 0.2 µm filter.

steps.title: Make phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS)
steps.instruction: Prepare PBS using sterile de‑ionised water with the following concentrations: 0.24 g L⁻¹ KH₂PO₄, 1.44 g L⁻¹ Na₂HPO₄, 0.20 g L⁻¹ KCl, 8.00 g L⁻¹ NaCl; adjust the pH to 7.4.

steps.title: Prepare mineral salts medium (MSM)
steps.instruction: Make MSM (pH 7.4) containing 0.20 g L⁻¹ ZnSO₄·7H₂O, 0.20 g L⁻¹ MgSO₄·7H₂O, 2.00 g L⁻¹ NH₄Cl, 1.50 g L⁻¹ KH₂PO₄, 9.00 g L⁻¹ Na₂HPO₄, 10.00 µg L⁻¹ CoSO₄·7H₂O, 3.00 g L⁻¹ MnSO₄·H₂O, 5.00 g L⁻¹ ferric citrate, 0.01 g L⁻¹ Titriplex III; sterilise before use.

steps.title: Design CCD experiment with five factors
steps.instruction: Using Design‑Expert software version 6.0, set up a central‑composite design (CCD) with the independent variables: agitation (rpm), temperature (°C), pH, inoculum volume (IV), and salinity. Generate 50 experimental runs for each PAH (phenanthrene and pyrene).

steps.title: Run biodegradation treatments (12 h incubation)
steps.instruction: Inoculate MSM with Cronobacter sakazakii MM045, add the appropriate PAH stock, and adjust agitation, temperature, pH and salinity according to each CCD run. Perform each treatment in triplicate and include an un‑inoculated MSM as a negative control. Incubate for 12 h.

steps.title: Harvest culture by centrifugation
steps.instruction: After the 12‑hour incubation, centrifuge each culture for 15 min at 4000 rpm and collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Extract metabolites with diethyl ether
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant, adjust its pH to 2.0, and transfer to a separating funnel. Perform liquid‑liquid extraction with diethyl ether, separate the ether layer, dry it over anhydrous sodium sulphate, filter, and concentrate the extract to a final volume of 3 ml.

steps.title: Purify extracts via silica gel chromatography
steps.instruction: Pack a column with silica gel, equilibrate with n‑hexane (mobile phase), load the 3 ml concentrated extract, elute with n‑hexane, collect the eluate, evaporate the solvent, and re‑dissolve the residue in 1 ml methanol for GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Analyze metabolites by GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µl of the methanol‑dissolved sample into a ThermoScientific TG‑5MS column (30 m × 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 µm film) using a split‑less injector (inlet 250 °C). Helium carrier gas flows at 1 ml min⁻¹. Hold the column at 50 °C for 3 min, then ramp at 10 °C min⁻¹ to 320 °C over 10 min. Acquire mass spectra in scan mode 35–500 u with a TQS Quantum XLS detector and identify metabolites by comparison with the NIST library.
